candidates.title: Privacy by design in WhatsApp
candidates.summary: Barry designed WhatsApp's server to relay answers without storing message text or transcriptions, keeping only minimal metadata and avoiding collection of special-category personal data.

candidates.quote: The server relays each answer in the same request and stores nothing. It keeps no message text and no transcriptions, and media is forwarded by reference and never downloaded.

candidates.title: Designing for end-of-life privacy
candidates.summary: Barry designed a system that never assumes a user's death, pausing and sending a check-in only to the custodian, with closing steps starting only after family confirmation.
candidates.heading: 🌸 In My Time > Privacy by design: the "shallow room" > Designing for the end of life
candidates.quote: The system never assumes a death. If an author goes quiet, it pauses patiently, then sends one gently worded check-in to the custodian, never to the author.

candidates.title: Secure AWS Access in CI Pipeline
candidates.summary: Barry implemented short-lived AWS credentials via GitHub OIDC in CI, separated roles for plan and apply stages, and restricted CI permissions to prevent privilege escalation.
candidates.heading: SECOM Semiconductor Pipeline > Security
candidates.quote: GitHub Actions signs in to AWS with GitHub OIDC: each run swaps a short-lived GitHub token for a one-hour IAM role session. Two CI roles. CI can't widen its own permissions.

candidates.title: Implementing least privilege access
candidates.summary: Barry configured identities with least privilege roles in code, disabled API keys, and used Microsoft Entra ID for authentication, ensuring the app refused to start without a secret key in production.
candidates.heading: Ask Barry > Security
candidates.quote: No API keys anywhere. API key access is switched off on both Azure resources... Least privilege, as code: the identities and roles live in `infra/identity.tf`, and tests fail if any identity gets a broad role such as Owner or Contributor.

candidates.title: CI AWS Role Verification
candidates.summary: Barry configured the CI pipeline to verify AWS access using an assumed role without stored keys, ensuring secure AWS interactions during pull requests and main branch pushes.
candidates.heading: Security design > Checking it
candidates.quote: The `terraform` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request and every push to `main`. It signs in with the plan role, runs `aws sts get-caller-identity`, then plans the runtime stack.

candidates.title: GitHub OIDC token exchange
candidates.summary: Barry configured GitHub Actions to request OIDC tokens and use AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, resolving an authorization failure by adding numeric repo IDs to trust policies.
candidates.heading: Security design > Keyless from the first commit > How the GitHub OIDC exchange works
candidates.quote: The first CI run failed with `Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` until the ID form was added.
